annotations.text: The column, with its key attached: small and faint at the bottom middle, standing exactly where the column will stand. The tap slides the column up out of that edge, and RESUME ends up breathing on the very pixels the key occupied; resuming hands the spot back. Esc does the same from a keyboard. Nothing pauses, and the ship stays live behind the thin wash.

Faint on purpose: the key lives inside the fight, so at rest it is furniture, not a control demanding to be read. It keeps the key box and the three bars, said small. PLAYERS keeps the corner it has always had; the corner row just loses MENU.
One drawn frame standing in for the motion: the column rising out of the bottom edge, LEAVE first because LEAVE lives at the top, the wash fading in with it.

On a phone the bottom middle is also the easiest reach there is: the key sits where a thumb already rests and the column rises into the same hand. Side becomes the corner panel's list here too when the zone holds more than two.

The corner panel, kept beside the column: the fight stays live and undimmed. Side is a list because a stepper walks: a row per side says them all at once, marks yours, and any other is one press, with the counts you weigh before switching riding along. The list carries over to the column's SIDE stop.
The roads not taken, kept for the record: the console center card with settings a page deeper, and the hold-and-flick radial that costs a new grammar.
